title: How to apply to Georgia campus vendor days
intro: Georgia schools that let community sellers in mostly do it through a student-life office: a market day, a tabling fair, or a homecoming/holiday market. Here is what they ask for and how to get approved fast.

sections.h: 1. Get a Georgia sales tax number first
p: Georgia says anyone who is a "dealer" (selling goods in Georgia) must register for a sales and use tax number and certificate of registration (O.C.G.A. § 48-8-59). Your Florida resale certificate does not cover Georgia.
Register online in the Georgia Tax Center (GTC) — choose "Register a New Business" and add Sales & Use Tax. Georgia DOR says the account number usually arrives by email within about 15 minutes.
Collect Georgia sales tax at the booth (4% state plus the local county rate) and file in GTC for each period you sell. Keep the certificate with you at the table; Georgia says it must be displayed.
Georgia's out-of-state exception covers convention and trade-show activity only — campus market days are not on that list, so register.

Georgia public schools (University System of Georgia) commonly ask for general liability of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence, with the school or the "Board of Regents of the University System of Georgia" named as additional insured. Georgia Tech calls this its Tier II insurance.
Ask your insurer for a certificate for each school, with that school's exact name as certificate holder / additional insured. It is usually free and quick.
Private colleges and technical colleges vary; some only ask for a business license.
Many schools (Clark Atlanta, Georgia Tech) ask for a business license. Bring your current local business tax receipt; renew it if it has lapsed.

Apply through the student-life / student-center office form on the school's page (links in each listing). Some list dates per semester (Georgia Southern Browses, Valdosta Third Thursdays); others are weekly (Clark Atlanta Market Thursdays, Spelman Market Friday, Georgia State Market Days).
Typical lead time: 1–2 weeks for a single market day; 6+ weeks for Georgia Tech activations; homecoming markets close a month or more before the event.
Payment: some take card online; Clark Atlanta takes cashier's check or money order only. No school logo items, no food unless you have food permits.
Some schools only allow outside sellers with a campus sponsor (UGA, Mercer). Those are marked "restricted".

Georgia sales tax certificate (GTC) · COI naming the school · business license · 3 real photos of the table and pieces · 10x10 tent, table and weights (or a 6-ft table where they provide one) · the dates you want.
